en.headline: Government relocates tribute flowers at Wang Fuk Court remembrance site
en.dek: Officials said the move creates space for more mourners while the flowers will be transferred to a religious venue for continued tribute.
body: The government said on Thursday night that it had relocated some of the flowers and tribute items left by the public at an open space near Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po to make room for people arriving after dark to pay their respects on the first anniversary of the deadly fire.

A spokesman said Civil Aid Service officers had placed bouquets in plastic containers and moved them to a nearby lawn at Kwong Fuk Sitting-out Area so that more people could continue to leave flowers while order and cleanliness were maintained.

The government said the flowers and related items would gradually be transferred to a religious venue for storage so that the public’s tributes could continue. Media liaison officers told people at the scene that the flowers would not be disposed of and would instead be moved to Fung Ying Seen Koon, a Taoist temple in Fanling.
Crowds continued to lay flowers and pay tribute at the site on Thursday evening, one year after the fire that killed 168 people.

zh.headline: 政府搬移宏福苑掉念地點花束 腾出空間供市民繼續致意
zh.dek: 政府指花束數量多，故以膠箱暫時放置並移至隣近草地，其後將逐步移送宗教場所存放。
body: 政府發言人周四晚上表示，由於大埔宏福苑週邊掉念地點花束數量多，考慮到傍晚可能有較多市民前往獻花，因以膠箱暫時放置部分花束及物品，並移至隣近草地，以腾出更多空間方便市民繼續致意。
發言人指，民安隊人員協助將花束放入膠箱並移到廣福公園休憩處隣近草地，保持場地整潔及秩序，確保市民每一份心意均得到尊重。
政府表示，隨著掉念花束漸多，為妥善保存各界掉念心意，將逐步把相關花束及物品移送至宗教場所存放，延續追思。警方媒體聯絡人員於現場告知市民，花束不會被清除，而會移送至粉嶺一間道教宮觀。
周四入夜後，仍有市民前往宏福苑週邊獻花掉念，記住一年前造成168人死亡的火災。
